title: Grateful Dead Live at Campus Stadium, UC Santa Barbara on 1974-05-25
source: Matrix: 60%sbd/40% aud; Sources: Master Soundboard Reel > Dick Latvala's Cassette > DAT > mastered to CD-R on an HHB CDR-850 > .shn (shnid 2635) Originally seeded to phlash.etree.org by Johnathan Miller. FOB Audience Recording by Jeremy Witt (shnid 111301) Preserved in posterity for 36 years by Jay Abrams (jra-sm) Recording Equipment: Sony TC-152, Sony Mics, BASF 120 minute cassettes, Dolby B Analog to Analog Transfer June 1974: Sony TC-152 -> Teac 1230 - Scotch 150, 7" Reels at 3 3/4 ips Transfer by Jim Blackwood Dec 23 2010 Editing and Mastering by Jamie Waddell on the GEMS Edit Station at 24 bit 96 kHz Weiss-Saracon for 16 bit 44.1kHz conversion   TLH for FLAC8   SBE Free

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1974 show captured in a solid matrix that adds depth and clarity, though the treble can be harsh for some ears.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its blistering tempos and fire, with Set 2 singled out as one of the best ever and standout moments on Scarlet Begonias, China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, U.S. Blues and more. The matrix blend generally improves balance—bringing punch to Phil’s bass and clearer guitar tones—but a few listeners find the high‑end harsh and biting. Overall the show shines despite minor tonal quirks in the recording.

ai_rating.rationale: Three 5‑star reviews and one 4‑star review emphasize an exceptional performance; recording quality is mostly praised but noted as a bit harsh, leading to a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Matrix blend adds depth and balances instruments, giving clearer bass and guitar; however some listeners describe the treble as harsh, biting, and somewhat unforgiving.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set bursts with high‑energy, fast‑tempo renditions; the second set is hailed as one of the best ever, providing a powerful climax to an already fiery night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Matrix makes his solo notes clearer and his rapid finger work more audible.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass gains extra punch and definition from the audience‑board blend.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano playing is highlighted as extraordinary on U.S. Blues, Mexicali Blues and Scarlet Begonias.
